notes: Nothing is built yet beyond the findings, repayments and fines. The approach will be built on the existing decision, event and knowledge records once the shape is known; its rates stay marked placeholders until answered.
question: When a candidate or official has a public record of misusing money or other ethics findings, who in real politics tends to approach them for corrupt or quiet arrangements (wealthy donors, business owners with matters before them, lobbyists, media owners), what do they typically offer (money through committees or outside groups, jobs for relatives, favorable coverage) and ask in return (votes, contracts, appointments), and how are such arrangements usually discovered?
requestedBy: Consequences for corruption and laws thread

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Covers exposure of misconduct, not who seeks out an already-exposed official.

title: Who approaches a candidate known to be corrupt, and with what
usableAnswer: A short list of approacher kinds with what each typically offers and wants, rough conditions that make an approach likelier (public finding, office with contracts or regulation, financial trouble), and the usual discovery routes, so the game can build the approach and its exposure from real patterns.
whyItMatters: The owner asked on 2026-09-22 that being corrupt also open opportunities: a mogul who sees you are corrupt might approach you with more money or offer to work together behind the scenes. Building that without a researched basis would mean inventing who approaches, what they offer and how often.
